fr.literal: transports-aussi pratiques-et, tard-le-soir-jusqu'à porte ouverte magasins [sujet] nombreux-parce-que

en.meaning: Still, the rent in Seoul is way too high, you know.
en.note: 월세 = monthly rent; Korean rentals also need a large deposit (보증금). 그래도 = even so.

fr.meaning: N'empêche, à Séoul, le loyer est beaucoup trop cher, tu sais bien.
fr.note: 월세 (wolse) = le loyer mensuel ; en Corée, il faut aussi verser une grosse caution (보증금). 그래도 = n'empêche, malgré tout.

en.meaning: That's true. Rent really is expensive.
en.note: 그건 그래 = 'that, yes, is so': you grant the point. 비싸 = 비싸요 without 요.

fr.meaning: Ça, c'est vrai. Le loyer, c'est vraiment cher.
fr.note: 그건 그래 = « ça, c'est bien ainsi » : on concède le point. 비싸 = 비싸요 sans le 요 de politesse.

en.meaning: Right, I'll give you that.
en.note: 맞아 = right (polite: 맞아요). 인정 = 'I admit it': very common among young Seoulites.

fr.meaning: C'est vrai, je te l'accorde.
fr.note: 맞아 = c'est juste (poli : 맞아요). 인정 (injeong) = « je reconnais » : très courant chez les jeunes Séoulites.

titles.fr: Une bonne affaire au marché de Namdaemun

sceneNotes.en: Ji-su, the neighbour you met on your first morning, is now a close friend you speak 반말 with; she spots your new bag, and you tell her how you haggled for it.
sceneNotes.fr: Ji-su, la voisine rencontrée le premier matin, est devenue une amie proche que vous tutoyez ; elle remarque votre nouveau sac, et vous lui racontez comment vous l'avez marchandé.

en.meaning: Oh, a new bag! Where did you get it?
en.note: -네 (casual -네요) notices something new. 샀어 is the casual past of 사다, to buy.

fr.meaning: Oh, un nouveau sac ! Tu l'as acheté où ?
fr.note: -네 (le -네요 familier) remarque une nouveauté. 샀어 est le passé familier de 사다, acheter.

en.meaning: I bought it yesterday afternoon at Namdaemun Market.
en.note: 어제 = yesterday; 오후 = afternoon; 그저께 = the day before yesterday. Namdaemun is Seoul's oldest and biggest traditional market.

fr.meaning: Je l'ai acheté hier après-midi au marché de Namdaemun.
fr.note: 어제 (eoje) = hier ; 오후 = l'après-midi ; 그저께 = avant-hier. Namdaemun est le plus ancien et le plus grand marché traditionnel de Séoul.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: 근데 가격 깎으려고 말하는 거, 한국어로 뭐라고 해?

forms.text: 근데 가격 깎으려고 말하는 거, 한국어로 뭐라고 해?
geunde gagyeok kkakkeuryeogo malhaneun geo, hangugeoro mworago hae?

en.meaning: By the way, what do you call talking the price down, in Korean?
en.note: X 한국어로 뭐라고 해? = how do you say X in Korean? When the word is missing, describe it. Polite: 뭐라고 해요?
en.literal: by-the-way price to-cut talking thing, Korean-in what-quote say

fr.meaning: Au fait, quand on discute pour faire baisser le prix, ça se dit comment en coréen ?
fr.note: X 한국어로 뭐라고 해 ? = comment dit-on X en coréen ? Quand le mot manque, décrivez-le. Vous connaissez déjà 깎다 (baisser le prix) depuis le marché du chapitre 1.
fr.literal: au-fait prix pour-baisser parler chose, coréen-en quoi-citation dit

en.meaning: It's called heungjeong, haggling. Did you haggle?
en.note: X(이)라고 해 = it's called X. 흥정하다 = to haggle, still normal in traditional markets but not in shops.

fr.meaning: On dit « heungjeong », marchander. Tu as marchandé ?
fr.note: X(이)라고 해 = ça s'appelle X. 흥정하다 = marchander : courant dans les marchés traditionnels, pas dans les magasins.

en.meaning: Yeah, at first it was 40,000 won, but I haggled.
en.note: -었는데 sets the scene for what follows: 'it was X, and then…'. 처음에는 = at first.

fr.meaning: Oui, au début c'était 40 000 wons, mais j'ai marchandé.
fr.note: -었는데 plante le décor de ce qui suit : « c'était X, et alors… ». 처음에는 (cheoeumeneun) = au début. 원이었는데 se prononce « wo-ni-on-neun-dé ».

en.meaning: Wow, so how much did you pay?
en.note: 얼마에 = for how much. 그래서 = so, and then.

fr.meaning: Waouh, et tu l'as eu pour combien ?
fr.note: 얼마에 = pour combien. 그래서 (geuraeseo) = et alors, du coup.

en.meaning: In the end I got it for 30,000 won.
en.note: 결국 = in the end. Price + 에 사다 = to buy for (a price).

fr.meaning: Finalement, je l'ai eu pour 30 000 wons.
fr.note: 결국 (gyeolguk) = finalement. Prix + 에 사다 = acheter pour (tel prix).

en.meaning: Oh, no wait. It was 25,000 won.
en.note: 아, 아니다 = 'oh no, wait': the casual way to correct yourself. 이었어 is the casual past of 이에요.

fr.meaning: Ah non, attends. C'était 25 000 wons.
fr.note: 아, 아니다 = « ah non, attends » : la façon familière de se corriger. 이었어 est le passé familier de 이에요. 25 000 = « deux dix-mille, cinq mille ».

en.meaning: Amazing! You really know how to haggle!
en.note: 대박 = 'awesome!', hugely common in casual speech. 잘했네 = you did well (with surprise).

fr.meaning: Trop fort ! Tu sais vraiment marchander !
fr.note: 대박 (daebak) = « génial ! », omniprésent à l'oral familier. 잘했네 = tu t'en es bien sorti (avec surprise).

en.meaning: Yeah, I was pretty proud of myself!
en.note: 뿌듯하다 = to feel proud and satisfied, after something you achieved.

fr.meaning: Oui, j'étais assez fier (fière) de moi !
fr.note: 뿌듯하다 (ppudeutada) = être fier et content de soi, après une réussite. Le ㅃ est un p tendu, sans souffle.

en.meaning: So, this happened the evening before yesterday.
en.note: 있었던 일 = something that happened. The trailing -인데 announces that a story is coming.

fr.meaning: Alors voilà, ça s'est passé avant-hier soir.
fr.note: 있었던 일 = une chose qui s'est passée. Le -인데 en suspens annonce qu'un récit arrive. 그저께 (geujeokke) = avant-hier.

titles.fr: Se débrouiller au quotidien à Séoul

notes: AI-assisted draft of chapter 4 for Korean (ko); native review required before publishing.

Polite 해요체 throughout, with honorific -(으)세요 when addressing people, as in chapters 1–3: everyone here is a stranger or a service provider. Staff use the formal 합니다 style and humble or honorific forms the learner only needs to understand (고객님, 도와드릴까요, 구매하셨어요, 불편을 드려서 죄송합니다); the learner uses 합니다 only in set formulas (실례합니다, 감사합니다, 알겠습니다 with the doctor). The of_course and tomorrow slots (neutral in the blueprint) are polite lines, labelled so.

Wordings to check first: 세탁기는 어디 있어요? as the where_is question when visiting a studio, 이 소포 좀 보내려고 하는데요, 여기 있어요, 카드요 for paying at the post office, 식후면 밥 먹고 바로요?, 선생님, 안녕하세요 for the greet_time_of_day slot (Korean has no time-specific greeting), 제 캐리어가 안 나왔어요.

Romanization follows chapters 1–3 (mangwonnyeogeseo and jihacheollyeogeseo with the inserted n, balgo for 밝고, gwallibi for 관리비, tensification not shown). 프랑스 is a sample home country to be swapped; nothing in the learner's lines depends on the learner's gender.

Facts to verify: a 5-million-won deposit and 650,000 won a month for a one-room in Mangwon-dong, 30,000 won to airmail 2 kg to France with about a week in transit, the 식후 30분 instruction on prescriptions, 30,000 won a month for an amateur football club with a free first month, airlines delivering delayed bags to the hotel.

characters.name: 정희
characters.personality: brisk landlady who lives on the ground floor, proud of her well-kept building

characters.name: 동수
characters.personality: meticulous, patient, always mentions the faster option

characters.name: 수빈
characters.personality: apologetic, efficient, sticks to the store's procedure

characters.name: 태호
characters.personality: gentle neighbourhood doctor who explains slowly and clearly

characters.name: 상우
characters.personality: energetic, welcoming, always looking for players for Saturday's match

characters.name: 유리
characters.personality: calm, formal, used to delivering bad news gently

sceneNotes.en: A small, bright one-room flat on the third floor of a building with no lift in Mangwon-dong, near the Han River; the landlady lives on the ground floor.
sceneNotes.fr: Un petit studio lumineux au troisième étage d'un immeuble sans ascenseur à Mangwon-dong, près du fleuve Han ; la propriétaire habite au rez-de-chaussée.

en.meaning: Come in. This is the room.
en.note: A 원룸 ('one-room') is the classic studio flat for students and young workers. Take your shoes off at the door.

fr.meaning: Entrez. Voici la chambre.
fr.note: Le 원룸 (« one-room ») est le studio typique des étudiants et des jeunes actifs. On se déchausse à l'entrée.

expressions.speaker: learner

en.meaning: The room is bright and clean.
en.note: Adjective stem + 고 = and: 밝고 깨끗하다, bright and clean. -네요 comments on what you see.

fr.meaning: La chambre est lumineuse et propre.
fr.note: Radical + 고 = et : 밝고 깨끗하다, lumineux et propre. -네요 commente ce que l'on constate. 밝고 se prononce « bal-go ».

expressions.pronunciationNote: 밝고 is said bal-go; 깨끗하네요 is kkae-kkeu-ta-ne-yo.

en.meaning: How much is the monthly rent?
en.note: 월세 = monthly rent, the word 지훈 complained about in chapter 3.

fr.meaning: Le loyer est de combien ?
fr.note: 월세 (wolse) = le loyer mensuel, le mot dont 지훈 se plaignait au chapitre 3.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: 보증금 오백만 원에 월세 육십오만 원이에요.

forms.text: 보증금 오백만 원에 월세 육십오만 원이에요.
bojeunggeum obaengman wone wolse yuksiboman wonieyo.

en.meaning: A 5-million-won deposit, and 650,000 won a month.
en.note: Rent comes with a large deposit (보증금), returned when you leave. 만 = 10,000: 오백만 = 500 ten-thousands; 육십오만 = 65 ten-thousands.
en.literal: deposit five-hundred-ten-thousand won-at monthly-rent sixty-five-ten-thousand won-is

fr.meaning: 5 millions de wons de caution, et 650 000 wons par mois.
fr.note: Le loyer s'accompagne d'une grosse caution (보증금), rendue au départ. 만 = 10 000 : 오백만 = 500 fois dix mille, 5 millions ; 육십오만 = 65 fois dix mille, 650 000.
fr.literal: caution cinq-cents-dix-mille wons-avec loyer soixante-cinq-dix-mille wons-c'est

en.meaning: Where's the washing machine?
en.note: Most studios come furnished with a washing machine, a fridge and air conditioning. 어디 있어요? = where is it?

fr.meaning: Où est la machine à laver ?
fr.note: La plupart des studios sont équipés d'une machine à laver, d'un frigo et de la climatisation. 어디 있어요 ? = où est-ce ?

en.meaning: It's on the balcony. There's air conditioning and a fridge too.
en.note: (이)랑 = and, between nouns, in speech. 에어컨 = air conditioner, a Konglish shortening.

fr.meaning: Elle est sur le balcon. Il y a aussi la clim et un frigo.
fr.note: (이)랑 = et, entre deux noms, à l'oral. 에어컨 = le climatiseur, abréviation à la coréenne de « air conditioner ».

en.meaning: Is it far from the subway station?
en.note: 에서 = from. Flat listings always give the walking time from the nearest station.

fr.meaning: C'est loin de la station de métro ?
fr.note: 에서 = depuis. Les annonces indiquent toujours le temps de marche depuis la station la plus proche.

en.meaning: And from when could I move in?
en.note: 들어오다 = to come in, to move in. 언제부터 = from when.

fr.meaning: Et je pourrais emménager à partir de quand ?
fr.note: 들어오다 = entrer, emménager. 언제부터 (eonjebuteo) = à partir de quand.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: 망원역에서 걸어서 오 분이에요. 다음 달 초부터 들어오시면 돼요.

forms.text: 망원역에서 걸어서 오 분이에요. 다음 달 초부터 들어오시면 돼요.
mangwonnyeogeseo georeoseo o bunieyo. daeum dal chobuteo deureoosimyeon dwaeyo.

en.meaning: It's five minutes' walk from Mangwon station. You can move in from early next month.
en.note: An n slips in before 역: mangwon-nyeok. 초 = the beginning (of a month or year); 말 = the end.
en.literal: Mangwon-station-from walking five minute-is. next month beginning-from come-in(honorific)-if fine

fr.meaning: C'est à cinq minutes à pied de Mangwon. Vous pouvez emménager début du mois prochain.
fr.note: Un n s'intercale devant 역 : « mangwon-nyeok ». 초 (cho) = le début (du mois, de l'année) ; 말 = la fin.
fr.literal: Mangwon-station-depuis à-pied cinq minutes-est. prochain mois début-dès entrer(honorifique)-si ça-va

en.meaning: I like it. I'll take this room.
en.note: 마음에 들다 = to like (literally 'to enter the heart'). (으)로 할게요 = I'll go for: the choice pattern from chapter 2's 이걸로 할게요.

fr.meaning: Elle me plaît. Je prends cette chambre.
fr.note: 마음에 들다 = plaire (mot à mot « entrer dans le cœur »). (으)로 할게요 = je choisis…, comme le 이걸로 할게요 du chapitre 2.

expressions.speaker: learner

en.meaning: Do I pay the maintenance fee separately?
en.note: 관리비 covers the building's upkeep and sometimes internet and water. 따로 = separately.

fr.meaning: Les charges, je les paie à part ?
fr.note: 관리비 = les charges (entretien de l'immeuble, parfois internet et eau). 따로 (ttaro) = à part. ㄴ devant ㄹ devient l : « gwal-li-bi ».

expressions.pronunciationNote: 관리비 is said gwal-li-bi: ㄴ before ㄹ becomes l.

en.meaning: It's a bit small, but it's fine.
en.note: -지만 = but. 좁다 = cramped (rooms, streets); 작다 = small (objects).

fr.meaning: C'est un peu petit, mais ça va.
fr.note: -지만 = mais. 좁다 = exigu (pièce, rue) ; 작다 = petit (objet). 괜찮네요 se prononce « gwen-tchan-né-yo ».

sceneNotes.en: The counter of the post office in Mangwon-dong; you are sending a two-kilo box of gifts to your family in France, and the clerk mentions a faster option.
sceneNotes.fr: Au guichet du bureau de poste de Mangwon-dong ; vous envoyez à votre famille en France un carton de cadeaux de deux kilos, et le guichetier vous parle d'une option plus rapide.

en.meaning: I'd like to send this parcel.
en.note: Verb + (으)려고 하는데요 = I'm planning to…: the trailing -는데요 leaves the request open, which sounds polite.

fr.meaning: Je voudrais envoyer ce colis.
fr.note: Verbe + (으)려고 하는데요 = « j'ai l'intention de… » : le -는데요 final laisse la demande en suspens, ce qui est poli. 소포 (sopo) = le colis.

en.meaning: Which country are you sending it to?
en.note: (으)로 = to, towards. 보내세요 is the honorific 'you send'.

fr.meaning: Vous l'envoyez dans quel pays ?
fr.note: (으)로 = vers, à destination de. 보내세요 = vous envoyez, à la forme honorifique.

en.meaning: To Paris, France, please.
en.note: Country then city, from big to small, as in Korean addresses. Swap in your own: 영국 (UK), 미국 (US), 캐나다 (Canada).

fr.meaning: Pour Paris, en France, s'il vous plaît.
fr.note: Le pays puis la ville, du plus grand au plus petit, comme dans les adresses coréennes. Mettez les vôtres : 벨기에 (Belgique), 스위스 (Suisse), 캐나다 (Canada).

en.meaning: How much is the postage?
en.note: 요금 = a fee or charge (postage, fares, bills); 가격 is the price of goods.

fr.meaning: Ça coûte combien d'affranchissement ?
fr.note: 요금 (yogeum) = un tarif (port, billet, facture) ; 가격, c'est le prix d'un article.

en.meaning: It's two kilos, so that's 30,000 won by airmail.
en.note: Weights take Sino-Korean numbers: 이 킬로, two kilos. 항공 = airmail; 선편 = sea mail. -니까 = since.

fr.meaning: Il fait deux kilos, donc ça fait 30 000 wons par avion.
fr.note: Les poids se disent avec les nombres sino-coréens : 이 킬로, deux kilos. 항공 (hanggong) = par avion ; 선편 = par bateau. -니까 = puisque.

en.meaning: How many days does it take?
en.note: 며칠 = how many days. 걸리다 = to take (time), as in chapter 1's 십 분쯤 걸려요.

fr.meaning: Ça prend combien de jours ?
fr.note: 며칠 (myeochil) = combien de jours. 걸리다 = prendre (du temps), comme dans le 십 분쯤 걸려요 du chapitre 1.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: 일주일쯤 걸려요. 더 빠른 것도 있는데, 좀 비싸요.

forms.text: 일주일쯤 걸려요. 더 빠른 것도 있는데, 좀 비싸요.
iljuiljjeum geollyeoyo. deo ppareun geotdo inneunde, jom bissayo.

en.meaning: About a week. There's a faster one too, but it's a bit expensive.
en.note: The faster option is EMS, international express mail. -는데 here means 'but'.
en.literal: one-week-about takes. more fast thing-also exists-but, a-bit expensive

fr.meaning: Une semaine environ. Il y a plus rapide, mais c'est un peu cher.
fr.note: L'option rapide, c'est l'EMS, le courrier express international. Ici, -는데 veut dire « mais ». 있는데 se prononce « in-neun-dé ».
fr.literal: une-semaine-environ prend. plus rapide chose-aussi il-y-a-mais, un-peu cher

en.meaning: No, I'll go with airmail.
en.note: (으)로 할게요 = I'll go for: it turns down the dearer option politely by simply choosing.

fr.meaning: Non, je prends l'envoi par avion.
fr.note: (으)로 할게요 = je choisis… : on refuse l'option plus chère en choisissant simplement l'autre.

en.meaning: Here you are, by card.
en.note: 여기 있어요 = here you are, as you hand something over. Adding 요 to a single noun keeps it polite.

fr.meaning: Voilà, par carte.
fr.note: 여기 있어요 = voilà, en tendant quelque chose. Ajouter 요 à un nom isolé suffit à rester poli, comme 편도요 au chapitre 2.

en.meaning: Roughly when will it arrive?
en.note: 언제쯤 = around when. 도착하다 = to arrive.

fr.meaning: Il arrive vers quand ?
fr.note: 언제쯤 = vers quand. 도착하다 = arriver ; 도착해요 se prononce « do-tcha-kè-yo ».

titles.fr: Un casque qui ne marche que d'un côté

sceneNotes.en: The service desk of an electronics store in Yongsan; the headphones you bought last Saturday make no sound on one side, and the assistant asks for the receipt.
sceneNotes.fr: Au comptoir du service client d'un magasin d'électronique de Yongsan ; le casque acheté samedi dernier ne fait plus de son d'un côté, et la vendeuse vous demande le ticket de caisse.

en.meaning: Hello. Is there a problem?
en.note: 무슨 = what kind of; 문제 = problem. 있으세요 is the honorific 'do you have'.

fr.meaning: Bonjour. Il y a un problème ?
fr.note: 무슨 = quel genre de ; 문제 (munje) = problème. 있으세요 = vous avez, à la forme honorifique.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: 이 헤드폰이 한쪽에서 소리가 안 나요.

forms.text: 이 헤드폰이 한쪽에서 소리가 안 나요.
i hedeuponi hanjjogeseo soriga an nayo.

en.meaning: These headphones make no sound on one side.
en.note: 소리가 나다 = a sound comes out; 안 makes it negative. 한쪽 = one side.
en.literal: this headphone [subject] one-side-from sound [subject] not comes-out

fr.meaning: Ce casque ne fait pas de son d'un côté.
fr.note: 소리가 나다 = un son sort ; 안 le rend négatif. 한쪽 (hanjjok) = un côté. Le ㅉ est un « tch » tendu.
fr.literal: ce casque [sujet] un-côté-de son [sujet] ne-pas sort

en.meaning: When did you buy them?
en.note: 구매하다 is the formal word for 'to purchase' used by staff; you just say 사다.

fr.meaning: Vous l'avez acheté quand ?
fr.note: 구매하다 = acheter, le mot soutenu du personnel ; vous, dites simplement 사다.

en.meaning: I bought them last Saturday.
en.note: 지난 = last: 지난주, last week; 지난달, last month. 샀어요 = I bought.

fr.meaning: Je l'ai acheté samedi dernier.
fr.note: 지난 (jinan) = dernier : 지난주, la semaine dernière ; 지난달, le mois dernier. 샀어요 = j'ai acheté.

en.meaning: We're sorry for the inconvenience. Do you have the receipt?
en.note: 불편을 드려서 죄송합니다 = sorry for the trouble: the standard staff apology. 영수증 = receipt.

fr.meaning: Désolés pour le désagrément. Vous avez le ticket de caisse ?
fr.note: 불편을 드려서 죄송합니다 = désolés du dérangement : l'excuse type du personnel. 영수증 (yeongsujeung) = le reçu.

en.meaning: Not at all, it's fine. Here it is.
en.note: 아니에요 waves the apology away; 괜찮아요 = it's all right. 여기 있어요 as you hand over the receipt.

fr.meaning: Mais non, ce n'est rien. Le voici.
fr.note: 아니에요 balaie l'excuse ; 괜찮아요 = ce n'est pas grave. 여기 있어요 en tendant le reçu.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: 교환이나 환불 중에 어떤 걸로 해 드릴까요?

forms.text: 교환이나 환불 중에 어떤 걸로 해 드릴까요?
gyohwanina hwanbul junge eotteon geollo hae deurilkkayo?

en.meaning: Would you like an exchange or a refund?
en.note: (이)나 = or. 중에 = among. Verb + 아/어 드릴까요? = shall I do it for you?, the respectful offer from chapter 2.
en.literal: exchange-or refund among which thing-as do give(humble)-shall-I

fr.meaning: Vous préférez un échange ou un remboursement ?
fr.note: (이)나 = ou. 중에 = parmi. Verbe + 아/어 드릴까요 ? = « voulez-vous que je le fasse pour vous ? », l'offre respectueuse vue au chapitre 2.
fr.literal: échange-ou remboursement parmi quel chose-en faire donner(humble)-dois-je

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: 새 걸로 바꿔 주실 수 있어요?

forms.text: 새 걸로 바꿔 주실 수 있어요?
sae geollo bakkwo jusil su isseoyo?

en.meaning: Could you swap them for a new pair?
en.note: 바꾸다 = to change, to swap. -아/어 주실 수 있어요? = could you (kindly) do it?: a polite request with honorific -시-.
en.literal: new thing-as change give(honorific) possibility exists

fr.meaning: Vous pouvez me l'échanger contre un neuf ?
fr.note: 바꾸다 = changer, échanger. -아/어 주실 수 있어요 ? = pourriez-vous… ? : une demande polie, avec le -시- honorifique.
fr.literal: neuf chose-en changer donner(honorifique) possibilité il-y-a

en.meaning: Thank you for sorting it out so quickly.
en.note: 처리하다 = to handle, to deal with. 빨리 = quickly: speed of service, 빨리빨리, is a point of pride in Korea.

fr.meaning: Merci d'avoir réglé ça si vite.
fr.note: 처리하다 = traiter, régler. 빨리 = vite : la rapidité du service, le fameux 빨리빨리, est une fierté coréenne.

en.meaning: I can't hear anything on the right side.
en.note: 들리다 = to be heard. 오른쪽 = right; 왼쪽 = left.

fr.meaning: Je n'entends rien du côté droit.
fr.note: 들리다 = être entendu. 오른쪽 = droite ; 왼쪽 (oenjjok) = gauche.

en.meaning: Could I have a refund?
en.note: 환불 = refund. Most shops refund within a week or two with the receipt.

fr.meaning: Vous pouvez me rembourser ?
fr.note: 환불 (hwanbul) = remboursement. La plupart des magasins remboursent sous une à deux semaines, sur présentation du reçu.

sceneNotes.en: A small neighbourhood clinic (내과) in Mangwon-dong; you have had a sore throat and a slight fever for two days, and the doctor prescribes medicine to take three times a day.
sceneNotes.fr: Dans un cabinet de quartier (내과) à Mangwon-dong ; mal de gorge et un peu de fièvre depuis deux jours : le médecin vous prescrit un médicament à prendre trois fois par jour.

en.meaning: Hello, doctor.
en.note: Doctors, like teachers, are addressed as 선생님. Korean has one greeting for every time of day: 안녕하세요.

fr.meaning: Bonjour, docteur.
fr.note: On appelle les médecins, comme les enseignants, 선생님 (seonsaengnim). Le coréen n'a qu'une salutation pour toute la journée : 안녕하세요.

en.meaning: What seems to be the trouble?
en.note: Literally 'where is uncomfortable?': the doctor's standard opening question.

fr.meaning: Qu'est-ce qui ne va pas ?
fr.note: Mot à mot « où est-ce inconfortable ? » : la question d'ouverture habituelle du médecin. 불편하다 = inconfortable, gênant.

en.meaning: My throat hurts and I have a bit of a fever.
en.note: Body part + 이/가 아프다, as in chapter 2's 머리가 아파요. 열이 있어요 = I have a temperature ('there is fever').

fr.meaning: J'ai mal à la gorge et un peu de fièvre.
fr.note: Partie du corps + 이/가 아프다, comme 머리가 아파요 au chapitre 2. 열이 있어요 = j'ai de la fièvre (« il y a de la fièvre »). 목 (mok) veut dire à la fois gorge et cou.

en.meaning: Since when has it been like that?
en.note: 언제부터 = since when. 그랬어요 = it was like that (past of 그래요).

fr.meaning: C'est comme ça depuis quand ?
fr.note: 언제부터 = depuis quand. 그랬어요 = c'était ainsi (passé de 그래요).

en.meaning: Since two days ago.
en.note: Days have native words: 하루 (one day), 이틀 (two), 사흘 (three). 전 = ago; 부터 = since.

fr.meaning: Depuis deux jours.
fr.note: Les durées en jours ont des mots natifs : 하루 (un jour), 이틀 (deux), 사흘 (trois). 전 = il y a ; 부터 = depuis. Le 요 final suffit à rester poli.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: 감기네요. 약은 하루 세 번, 식후에 드세요. 아시겠죠?

forms.text: 감기네요. 약은 하루 세 번, 식후에 드세요. 아시겠죠?
gamgineyo. yageun haru se beon, sikue deuseyo. asigetjyo?

en.meaning: It's a cold. Take the medicine three times a day, after meals. Is that clear?
en.note: 식후 = after meals; 식전 = before meals. 드세요 is the honorific 'take, eat'. You collect the medicine at the pharmacy next door with the prescription.
en.literal: cold(observing). medicine [topic] day three times, after-meal-at take(honorific). know(honorific)-right

fr.meaning: C'est un rhume. Prenez le médicament trois fois par jour, après les repas. C'est clair ?
fr.note: 식후 (siku) = après le repas ; 식전 = avant. 드세요 = prenez, à la forme honorifique. On retire ensuite les médicaments à la pharmacie voisine, avec l'ordonnance.
fr.literal: rhume(constat). médicament [thème] jour trois fois, après-repas-à prenez(honorifique). savez(honorifique)-hein

en.meaning: 'After meals', meaning right after eating?
en.note: X(이)면 = if it's X: here, 'if it's after meals, (does that mean)…'. 바로 = right away.

fr.meaning: « Après les repas », c'est-à-dire juste après avoir mangé ?
fr.note: X(이)면 = si c'est X : ici, « après les repas, ça veut dire… ». 바로 (baro) = tout de suite. 밥 (bap), le riz, désigne aussi le repas.

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: 아니요, 식사하고 삼십 분 뒤에 드세요.

forms.text: 아니요, 식사하고 삼십 분 뒤에 드세요.
aniyo, siksahago samsip bun dwie deuseyo.

en.meaning: No, take it thirty minutes after your meal.
en.note: Korean prescriptions often say 식후 30분, thirty minutes after meals. 뒤에 = after.
en.literal: no, meal-having-and thirty minutes after take(honorific)

fr.meaning: Non, prenez-le trente minutes après le repas.
fr.note: Les ordonnances coréennes indiquent souvent 식후 30분 : trente minutes après le repas. 뒤에 (dwie) = après.
fr.literal: non, repas-faire-et trente minutes après prenez(honorifique)

en.meaning: Yes, I understand. Three times a day.
en.note: 알겠습니다 is the formal 알겠어요: right for a doctor. Repeating the key point shows you have understood.

fr.meaning: Oui, j'ai compris. Trois fois par jour.
fr.note: 알겠습니다 est la version soutenue de 알겠어요 : de mise avec un médecin. Répéter le point clé montre que l'on a compris.

en.meaning: Thank you. Goodbye.
en.note: 안녕히 계세요 ('stay in peace') is what you say when you leave and the other person stays; 안녕히 가세요 when they leave.

fr.meaning: Merci. Au revoir.
fr.note: 안녕히 계세요 (« restez en paix ») se dit quand c'est vous qui partez et l'autre qui reste ; 안녕히 가세요 quand c'est l'autre qui s'en va.

en.meaning: I keep coughing.
en.note: 기침이 나다 = to cough. 계속 = continuously. A runny nose is 콧물이 나요.

fr.meaning: Je n'arrête pas de tousser.
fr.note: 기침이 나다 = tousser. 계속 (gyesok) = sans arrêt. Le nez qui coule : 콧물이 나요.

titles.fr: S'inscrire à un club de foot

sceneNotes.en: An amateur football club that trains on the pitch of Mangwon Han River Park on Tuesday and Thursday evenings; the coach invites you to Saturday's match.
sceneNotes.fr: Un club de foot amateur qui s'entraîne sur le terrain du parc du fleuve Han à Mangwon, le mardi et le jeudi soir ; l'entraîneur vous invite au match de samedi.

en.meaning: Good to see you! Is this your first time?
en.note: 반가워요 = I'm glad to see you, the friendly greeting from chapter 1's 만나서 반가워요. 처음 = the first time.

fr.meaning: Bienvenue ! C'est votre première fois ?
fr.note: 반가워요 = je suis content de vous voir, la salutation amicale du 만나서 반가워요 du chapitre 1. 처음 (cheoeum) = la première fois.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: 연습은 무슨 요일 몇 시에 해요?

forms.text: 연습은 무슨 요일 몇 시에 해요?
yeonseubeun museun yoil myeot sie haeyo?

en.meaning: Which days and what time is training?
en.note: 무슨 요일 = which day of the week; 몇 시 = what time. 연습 = practice, training.
en.literal: practice [topic] what-kind weekday what hour-at do

fr.meaning: L'entraînement, c'est quels jours et à quelle heure ?
fr.note: 무슨 요일 = quel jour de la semaine ; 몇 시 = quelle heure. 연습 (yeonseup) = l'entraînement. Une seule question pour le jour et l'heure.
fr.literal: entraînement [thème] quel jour quelle heure-à fait

en.meaning: Tuesdays and Thursdays at eight in the evening.
en.note: Days: 월 (Mon), 화 (Tue), 수 (Wed), 목 (Thu), 금 (Fri), 토 (Sat), 일 (Sun) + 요일. 저녁 = evening.

fr.meaning: Le mardi et le jeudi, à huit heures du soir.
fr.note: Les jours : 월 (lun.), 화 (mar.), 수 (mer.), 목 (jeu.), 금 (ven.), 토 (sam.), 일 (dim.) + 요일. 저녁 (jeonyeok) = le soir.

en.meaning: How much is the membership fee?
en.note: 회비 = membership fee (회 = club, association; 비 = fee, as in 관리비).

fr.meaning: La cotisation, c'est combien ?
fr.note: 회비 (hoebi) = la cotisation (회 = association ; 비 = frais, comme dans 관리비, les charges).

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: 한 달에 삼만 원이에요. 첫 달은 무료예요.

forms.text: 한 달에 삼만 원이에요. 첫 달은 무료예요.
han dare samman wonieyo. cheot dareun muryoyeyo.

en.meaning: It's 30,000 won a month. The first month is free.
en.note: 한 달에 = per month (에 = per). 첫 = first. 무료 = free of charge.
en.literal: one month-per thirty-thousand won-is. first month [topic] free-is

fr.meaning: C'est 30 000 wons par mois. Le premier mois est gratuit.
fr.note: 한 달에 = par mois (에 = par). 첫 = premier. 무료 (muryo) = gratuit.
fr.literal: un mois-par trente-mille wons-c'est. premier mois [thème] gratuit-c'est

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: 이번 주에 한번 같이 뛰어 봐도 돼요?

forms.text: 이번 주에 한번 같이 뛰어 봐도 돼요?
ibeon jue hanbeon gachi ttwieo bwado dwaeyo?

en.meaning: May I come and play with you once this week?
en.note: 뛰다 = to run, and also to play (a match). -아/어 봐도 돼요? = may I try…?, as in chapter 2's 입어 봐도 돼요?
en.literal: this week-in once together running try-even is-okay

fr.meaning: Je peux venir jouer avec vous une fois cette semaine ?
fr.note: 뛰다 = courir, et aussi jouer (un match). -아/어 봐도 돼요 ? = je peux essayer de… ?, comme 입어 봐도 돼요 ? au chapitre 2.
fr.literal: cette semaine-à une-fois ensemble courir essayer-même ça-va

en.meaning: Of course! There's a match on Saturday too; do you want to come?
en.note: 그럼요 = of course. 시합 = match, game. -ㄹ래요? = do you want to…?, the polite form of chapter 2's 갈래?

fr.meaning: Bien sûr ! Il y a aussi un match samedi, vous voulez venir ?
fr.note: 그럼요 (geureomyo) = bien sûr. 시합 = le match. -ㄹ래요 ? = vous voulez… ?, la forme polie du 갈래 ? du chapitre 2.

en.meaning: Great! I really love football.
en.note: 좋아요 = great, it's good; 좋아해요 = I like (something). 저 = the polite 'I'.

fr.meaning: Super ! J'adore le foot.
fr.note: 좋아요 = c'est bien, d'accord ; 좋아해요 = j'aime (quelque chose). 저 = le « je » poli. 축구 (chukgu) = le football.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: 그럼 화요일 저녁 여덟 시에 올게요.

forms.text: 그럼 화요일 저녁 여덟 시에 올게요.
geureom hwayoil jeonyeok yeodeol sie olgeyo.

en.meaning: Then I'll come on Tuesday at eight in the evening.
en.note: -ㄹ게요 = I'll (a promise to the listener): 올게요, I'll come. Repeating day and time confirms the plan.
en.literal: then Tuesday evening eight hour-at will-come

fr.meaning: Alors je viendrai mardi à huit heures du soir.
fr.note: -ㄹ게요 = je vais… (un engagement envers l'autre) : 올게요, je viendrai. Reprendre le jour et l'heure confirme le rendez-vous.
fr.literal: alors mardi soir huit heures-à viendrai

en.meaning: May I try it out for free?
en.note: 체험 = trying something out; clubs and gyms often offer a free 체험 session.

fr.meaning: Je peux faire un essai gratuit ?
fr.note: 체험 (cheheom) = l'essai, la découverte : clubs et salles de sport proposent souvent une séance d'essai gratuite.

sceneNotes.en: The baggage service desk at Incheon Airport; your flight from Paris landed an hour ago, but your big blue suitcase is still in Paris.
sceneNotes.fr: Au comptoir des bagages de l'aéroport d'Incheon ; votre vol en provenance de Paris a atterri il y a une heure, mais votre grande valise bleue est restée à Paris.

expressions.speaker: learner

en.meaning: Excuse me, sorry to bother you.
en.note: 실례합니다 ('I commit a discourtesy') is the formal 'excuse me' for interrupting staff or strangers.

fr.meaning: Excusez-moi de vous déranger.
fr.note: 실례합니다 (« je commets une impolitesse ») est le « excusez-moi » soutenu pour interrompre un employé ou un inconnu.

expressions.pronunciationNote: 실례 is said sil-lye: ㄹ and ㄹ make a long l.

en.meaning: Yes? How can I help you?
en.note: 고객님 (customer + 님) is how staff address you. 도와드릴까요 = shall I help you (humble).

fr.meaning: Oui ? Que puis-je faire pour vous ?
fr.note: 고객님 (client + 님) : c'est ainsi que le personnel s'adresse à vous. 도와드릴까요 = puis-je vous aider (forme humble).

en.meaning: My suitcase hasn't come out.
en.note: 캐리어 (from 'carrier') is what Koreans call a wheeled suitcase. 제 = my (polite). 나오다 = to come out.

fr.meaning: Ma valise n'est pas sortie.
fr.note: 캐리어 (de l'anglais « carrier ») : c'est ainsi qu'on appelle une valise à roulettes en Corée. 제 = mon, ma (poli). 나오다 = sortir.

en.meaning: Which flight did you come on?
en.note: 항공편 = flight. 오셨어요 = you came (honorific past of 오다).

fr.meaning: Vous êtes arrivé(e) par quel vol ?
fr.note: 항공편 (hanggongpyeon) = le vol. 오셨어요 = vous êtes venu(e), passé honorifique de 오다.

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: 한 시간 전에 도착한 파리 비행기예요.

forms.text: 한 시간 전에 도착한 파리 비행기예요.
han sigan jeone dochakan pari bihaenggiyeyo.

en.meaning: The plane from Paris that landed an hour ago.
en.note: A verb in -ㄴ before a noun describes it in the past: 도착한 비행기, 'the plane that arrived'. 시간 = hours (a duration).
en.literal: one hour ago arrived Paris plane-is

fr.meaning: L'avion de Paris qui a atterri il y a une heure.
fr.note: Un verbe en -ㄴ devant un nom le décrit au passé : 도착한 비행기, « l'avion qui est arrivé ». Pas de pronom relatif ! 시간 = heure (durée).
fr.literal: une heure avant arrivé Paris avion-est

expressions.speaker: character
expressions.text: 죄송합니다. 짐이 아직 파리에 있는 것 같습니다.

forms.text: 죄송합니다. 짐이 아직 파리에 있는 것 같습니다.
joesonghamnida. jimi ajik parie inneun geot gatseumnida.

en.meaning: We're sorry. It seems your luggage is still in Paris.
en.note: -는 것 같습니다 = it seems that…: staff use it to soften bad news. 짐 = luggage.
en.literal: sorry. luggage [subject] still Paris-in existing thing seems

fr.meaning: Nous sommes désolés. Il semble que votre bagage soit encore à Paris.
fr.note: -는 것 같습니다 = il semble que… : le personnel l'emploie pour adoucir une mauvaise nouvelle. 짐 (jim) = les bagages.
fr.literal: désolé. bagage [sujet] encore Paris-à existant chose semble

expressions.speaker: learner
expressions.text: 찾으면 명동에 있는 호텔로 보내 주세요.

forms.text: 찾으면 명동에 있는 호텔로 보내 주세요.
chajeumyeon myeongdonge inneun hotello bonae juseyo.

en.meaning: When you find it, please send it to my hotel in Myeongdong.
en.note: -(으)면 = if, when. 명동에 있는 호텔 = the hotel (that is) in Myeongdong. Airlines usually deliver delayed bags for free.
en.literal: if-find Myeongdong-in existing hotel-to send please

fr.meaning: Quand vous la retrouverez, envoyez-la à mon hôtel à Myeongdong, s'il vous plaît.
fr.note: -(으)면 = si, quand. 명동에 있는 호텔 = l'hôtel (qui se trouve) à Myeongdong. Les compagnies livrent en général gratuitement les bagages retardés.
fr.literal: si-trouvez Myeongdong-à se-trouvant hôtel-vers envoyez s'il-vous-plaît

en.meaning: Roughly when can I get it?
en.note: 받다 = to receive. -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요 = can.

fr.meaning: Je pourrai la récupérer vers quand ?
fr.note: 받다 (batda) = recevoir. -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요 = pouvoir.

en.meaning: It should get to your hotel tomorrow afternoon.
en.note: -ㄹ 거예요 = will (a prediction). 오후에는 = in the afternoon, at the latest.

fr.meaning: Elle devrait arriver à votre hôtel demain après-midi.
fr.note: -ㄹ 거예요 = futur, prévision. 오후에는 = dans l'après-midi, au plus tard.

en.meaning: Thank you so much for your help.
en.note: 도와주셔서 = because you helped (honorific). 정말 = really.

fr.meaning: Merci beaucoup pour votre aide.
fr.note: 도와주셔서 = parce que vous m'avez aidé(e) (honorifique). 정말 = vraiment.

en.meaning: I can't find my big blue suitcase.
en.note: 못 = can't. -겠어요 makes it softer: 'I can't seem to find'. Colour, then size, then the noun.

fr.meaning: Je ne trouve pas ma grande valise bleue.
fr.note: 못 = ne pas pouvoir. -겠어요 adoucit : « je n'arrive pas à trouver ». Couleur, taille, puis le nom : tout se place avant.
